title: Saʿd ibn Yūsuf comes of age at sixteen and takes the government into his own hands. The regency of Naṣr al-Istijjī ends
Naṣr al-Istijjī, regent for barely half a year, dies of 'sickness' in the days after the young sultan comes of age
source: Trent's account (in the days after 18 January 1364; exact date not given)

title: Sultan Saʿd takes a second wife: Duʿāʾ of the Marīnid house, twice widowed, his father's widow and minister. He comes to the throne with two wives, Aiman the Mamlūk and Duʿāʾ the Marīnid
source: Trent's account (soon after Naṣr's death; exact date not given)

title: The ʿulamāʾ are displeased with the young sultan: their satisfaction stands at 37% in the middle of the war

Saʿd summons the Jamāʿa and brings in reforms for the ʿulamāʾ. The tax on the dhimmīs, remitted since 1352, is collected again, and a new campaign of conversion begins. It is enough to keep the clergy from mutiny while the war goes on
